edits.before:
Marionette does not require a custom MCP server, a hosted AI chat, or a WebMCP
connection to build an application. A future local MCP wrapper would need to solve
a demonstrated client integration gap beyond reading these files. Keep tooling
outside the production import graph and avoid duplicating the contract in tool
prompts. The same documentation remains available to human readers.
edits.after:
Marionette does not require MCP or a hosted AI service to build an application.
The [documentation MCP setup guide](https://marionettejs.com/docs/mcp/) describes
the optional hosted HTTP and local stdio interfaces to the same verified corpus.
Read `marionette://catalog`, compare the exact installed version and source
revision, and pass that version to every tool. Unsupported versions are errors;
use the installed Markdown when the hosted snapshot does not match. Copying the
consumer skill does not automatically connect an MCP server.

The browser's WebMCP workshop operates its own running example. Hosted MCP only
retrieves documentation and recipe source; neither proves behavior in a consumer
application. Keep tooling outside the production import graph and use the
application's tests to verify its behavior.
